AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Robot surgery is new method that maintains advantages and overcomes disadvantages of conventional methods, even in pancreatic surgery. This study aimed to evaluate safety and benefits of robot-assisted minimally invasive pancreaticoduodenectomy (robot PD).

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: This study included 237 patients who underwent PD between 2015 and 2017. Demographics, surgical outcomes were evaluated.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Fifty-one patients underwent robot PD and 186 underwent open PD. Robot PD group had younger age (60.7 vs 65.4 years, p = 0.006) and lower BMI (22.7 vs 24.0, p = 0.007). Robot PD group had lower proportion of patients with firm or hard pancreatic texture (15.7% vs 38.2%, p = 0.004) and smaller pancreatic duct size (2.3 vs 3.3 mm, p = 0.002). Two groups had similar operation time (robot vs open: 335.6 vs 330.1 minutes) and complications (15.7% vs 21.0%), including postoperative pancreatic fistula rate (6.0% vs 12.0%). Robot PD group had lower postoperative pain score (3.7 vs 4.1 points, p = 0.008), and shorter postoperative stay (10.6 vs 15.3 days, p = 0.001).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Robot PD is comparable to open PD in early outcomes. Robot PD is safe and feasible and enables early recovery; indication for robot PD is expected to expand in the near future. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
